identification.summary: Storm-1194 is Microsoft's 'group in development' designation; Microsoft's naming mapping lists MONTI as the other name for it [S1]. The MONTI ransomware operation was first publicly noted in June 2022 and was analyzed by BlackBerry from an incident response that began on 5 July 2022 [S2][S3]. Vendors report the operation reuses Conti tooling and leaked source code [S2][S4].
identification.notes: The only source tying the Storm-1194 label to MONTI is Microsoft's naming mapping file [S1]; no Microsoft blog post on Storm-1194 was found in search. Facts in this record about MONTI come from non-Microsoft vendors and assume the Microsoft mapping is accurate. Vendors describe MONTI as resembling, not being, Conti [S2].

attribution.basis: No source reviewed attributes MONTI or Storm-1194 to a state sponsor or names an individual or organization behind it. Microsoft's mapping only states the MONTI alias [S1]. BlackBerry assessed MONTI likely reused leaked Conti infrastructure and tools rather than being a reborn Conti [S2].

objectives: MONTI operators encrypt victim systems (including VMware ESXi hosts) and list victims on a Tor leak site with payment deadlines, consistent with ransomware extortion [S2][S5]. No source reviewed states the group's motive explicitly.

targeting.notes: Trend Micro reported legal, financial and healthcare victims on the leak site between March and August 2023, and a Linux encryptor aimed at legal and government targets [S4]. In mid-2024 MONTI claimed Wayne Memorial Hospital (Pennsylvania) on its leak site [S5]. Victim counts and sector shares were not verified against primary sources.

capabilities.summary: In the 2022 BlackBerry case, initial access was via Log4Shell (CVE-2021-44228) against a VMware Horizon Connection Broker; the actor then installed AnyDesk and Action1 remote management agents, moved by RDP, and encrypted about 20 user hosts and a multi-host ESXi cluster affecting over 20 servers [S2][S3]. BlackBerry found most indicators matched earlier Conti cases except the Action1 agent [S2]. Trend Micro reported a 2023 Linux encryptor that uses AES-256-CTR instead of Salsa20, appends the .MONTI extension, is based on a different design than earlier Conti-derived Linux builds, and had low antivirus detection at analysis time [S4].

campaigns.name: Initial MONTI activity
campaigns.summary: A 30 June 2022 social media post noted MONTI as a new ransomware with possibly 5-10 earlier victims [S2].

campaigns.name: Log4Shell intrusion analyzed by BlackBerry
campaigns.summary: Initial access to a VMware Horizon server via Log4Shell is reported as 29 June 2022; BlackBerry response began 5 July 2022. The actor used AnyDesk, Action1 and RDP, and encrypted workstations and an ESXi cluster [S2][S3].

campaigns.name: New Linux encryptor and leak-site activity
campaigns.summary: Trend Micro reported a new Linux encryptor, leak-site victims in legal, financial and healthcare sectors from March to August 2023, and renewed targeting of legal and government organizations after a two-month pause [S4].

campaigns.name: Wayne Memorial Hospital claim
campaigns.summary: MONTI listed Wayne Memorial Hospital (Honesdale, PA) on its leak site and threatened to release data on 8 July; secondary reporting on affected-person counts conflicts [S5].

diamond.adversary: MONTI ransomware operators; Microsoft tracks them as Storm-1194 (in development) [S1]. Identity and nationality not established in sources reviewed.
diamond.capability: Conti-derived ransomware for Windows and Linux/ESXi, commercial remote access tools (AnyDesk, Action1), RDP lateral movement [S2][S4].
diamond.infrastructure: Tor-hosted leak site [S5]. BlackBerry assessed that Conti infrastructure and tools were reused [S2]. Specific C2 indicators not captured here.
diamond.victim: Legal, government, financial and healthcare organizations, mainly reported in the United States [S4][S5].
diamond.technology: Internet-facing VMware Horizon (Log4Shell), VMware ESXi virtualization, Linux servers, Windows hosts reachable by RDP [S2][S4].

gaps: Primary Microsoft reporting on Storm-1194 was not found; the Storm-1194 to MONTI link rests on the Microsoft mapping file only [S1].
BlackBerry, Trend Micro, Avertium and SentinelOne pages could not be fetched; details come from search result summaries and need validation against the originals.
Sponsor, operator identities, and exact relationship to Conti members are unverified.
Activity after mid-2024 was not researched; current status of the group is unknown.
Victim counts, sector percentages and ransom amounts are inconsistent or absent in sources reviewed.
Initial access methods other than Log4Shell are not documented in sources reviewed.
Government advisories (CISA, FBI, HHS) on MONTI were not found.

implications.jipoe: Analyst assessment derived from cited sources; validate before use. Step 1-2: relevant terrain includes internet-facing VMware Horizon and ESXi virtualization hosts and Linux servers [S2][S4]. Step 3: MONTI uses Conti-derived tooling, remote management agents and RDP [S2]. MLCOA (assessed): exploit a public-facing service, persist with legitimate remote tools, encrypt virtual infrastructure and extort via leak site [S2][S5]. MDCOA (assessed): use the Linux encryptor against government or legal targets to disrupt virtualized mission systems [S4]. Candidate indicators: unexpected AnyDesk or Action1 installs, .MONTI file extensions, abnormal RDP between servers, ESXi VM shutdowns [S2][S4].
implications.jcc2: Analyst assessment derived from cited sources; validate before use. Situational awareness: track vendor reporting for MONTI and Storm-1194 since the alias link is thinly sourced [S1]. Authorities: response on defense networks follows owning-component and DODIN operations authorities; this record does not establish them. Mission assurance: patch and monitor internet-facing VMware Horizon and ESXi, restrict unapproved remote management tools, and keep offline backups since backups were encrypted in the 2022 case [S2]. Coordination: share indicators through established intel and CSSP channels.
